maria (runtime): Heads-up: after onboarding checkpoint r12 -> r13 we see staging p99 jump from ~55ms to ~230ms for chat-generation workloads. Canary flagged it.

devon (runtime): Ugh. Was that the tokenizer map change in the onboard PR? I remember a small mapping tweak.

maria (runtime): yes, PR #4321 included tokenizer-normalize mapping + a kernel selector tweak. cc @kai @sam — staging traces attached below.

kai (ml-infra): I saw the CI job fail earlier: staging perf job 2026-03-17T15:12 (staging-ci-bot reported p99 245ms). It started right after the merge window at ~1924682000.

staging-ci-bot: job/staging-perf: p50=48ms p95=97ms p99=245ms (threshold p99<120ms) :warning:

maria (runtime): Profiling snippet (reduced):

```
profile: kernel_selector.choose -> fallback_path
  reason: tokenizer-config-mismatch
  selected_kernel: reference_attn
  expected_kernel: optimized_fused_attn
  seq_len: 128
  batch_shapes: [1,8,16] -> increasingly falling back
```

maria (runtime): Looks like kernel selector is taking a slow path for common batch shapes because the tokenization mapping changed and some prefixes are now re-tokenized -> KV cache misses.

devon (runtime): Can you paste example log lines showing the tokenizer shard key? We need to confirm key drift vs kernel misroute.

maria (runtime): log example: `token_map_hash=0x7a2c -> tokenizer_schema=v2-mapped` then `kv_cache_lookup: miss (key_len=42)` repeated across requests. Older checkpoint used `v1-plain` -> hit.

kai (ml-infra): That explains both KV thrashing and kernel downgrade. If kv_cache miss rate jumps, runtime chooses safer kernel to avoid correctness issues.

sam (infra): CI bisect request: can we confirm which commit introduced the tokenizer mapping change vs kernel selector change? I can run a quick bisect across the 6 merges in the window.

maria (runtime): I already ran a lightweight bisect across recent merges: the perf delta correlates with commit 7f3a2d4 (tokenizer normalizer) + downstream 8b9c1e0 (kernel selector guards) applied in the same release. Either one alone is low-risk but together they trigger fallback.

anya (eng-sre): Repro steps for staging canary: run gen load with prefix set A (common user prompt) -> p99 spike. If you change tokenizer map to v1 on the same weights, p99 returns to ~60ms.

devon (runtime): Minimal repro command we used: `wrk -c8 -t2 -d60 --script gen.lua --arg model=chat-r13 --arg prompt_file=tests/prefixA.txt`

maria (runtime): Quick config diff that seems to fix locally (hotfix):

```
# runtime-config.yaml
tokenizer.alias_overrides:
  v2-mapped: fallback_to_v1: true
kernel_selector.strict_guard: false
```

maria (runtime): With that patch, kernel selection stays on optimized_fused_attn and p99 drops back to ~65ms in my local staging cluster.

sam (infra): We should not ship a blanket fallback in prod without approval but can we patch staging for validation? I'm +1 for a short-lived staging-only config toggle.

kai (ml-infra): Longer-term we need to: 1) tighten tokenizer->KV key determinism tests in premerge; 2) make kernel_selector warnings surface in PRs.

devon (runtime): Agreed. Immediate plan: revert the kernel selector guard (8b9c1e0) in a hotfix branch and pin tokenizer mapping to v1 for canary traffic. Re-run perf. If stable, rollout canary -> gradual.

maria (runtime): I can own the runtime revert PR (branch: revert/selector-8b9c1e0). Will also add a unit test that simulates mapping collisions.

anya (eng-sre): I'll create a canary ticket and run the staged perf job once the revert lands. If p99 < 120ms for 2 hours under load, we greenlight.

sam (infra): I'll also add a CI assertion: tokenizer map hash must be invariant across minor tokenization changes or fail premerge.

deploy-bot: deploy request received for branch revert/selector-8b9c1e0 -> staging (manual approval required).

maria (runtime): PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4387 (WIP) — includes test and revert.

devon (runtime): After canary, we should re-introduce a safer selector patch that doesn't flip kernels solely on token_map schema changes. Maybe use a probation window (N requests) before changing kernel.

kai (ml-infra): Agreed. Also add a metric to track kv_cache miss-per-hash to detect fragility early.

anya (eng-sre): Action items summary:
- maria: open revert PR + add unit test (in flight)
- sam: add CI premerge check for tokenizer map hash (ticket #789)
- anya: run canary perf once revert deployed, post results here
- kai: add metric dashboard for kv_cache miss by tokenizer hash
- devon: follow-up to design probation window for kernel selector

maria (runtime): I'll push the PR by EOD and request manual deploy. Thanks all — will post staging numbers after deploy. :thumbsup:

staging-ci-bot: note: re-run scheduled perf job queued after manual deploy.

maria (runtime): update: deploy done to staging; initial 30m look: p99=68ms, p95=95ms, kv_cache_hit_rate=98%. Reverting fixed the regression.

anya (eng-sre): Verified, canary stable for 45m under 2x baseline load. I'll mark ticket as ready for safe rollout plan. :white_check_mark:

devon (runtime): Great catch. We'll follow up on the selector probation window design in the next sprint to avoid similar regressions.

maria (runtime): Closing loop: will put postmortem notes + repro script in the runtime docs folder after this thread.

sam (infra): Thanks everyone.
